payload.body:
Landed both halves. fleet/roles/implementer.md gains '## The state you reached' directly after '## The issue': the key state.reached, the one command `kata meta set $KATA_REF state.reached "{...}" --json-value` with the path as a placeholder, the two fields expected (path under state-exams/expected/) and content (the getContent() pair), and the three rules — after the task's own exam is green, 'post it once', and 'only a task whose Proof names a state exam'. Decision worth recording: the --json-value flag is named in prose AFTER the command block, because leg (a)'s regex wants --json-value before 'expected' and 'content' while the command string spells the fields first.

fleet/CONTRACT.md: one paragraph appended to the KATA_REF paragraph of the 'Kata record (engine)' bullet (not at the bullet's end, to stay clear of Task 2's likely append on the same file), naming state.reached, expected, content, the producing task's implementer as sole poster and the driver as sole reader, in that order. It deliberately does not spell Task 2's engine-side mechanics (the hub request, state-exams/posted/, the fact:state.reached event) — that is Task 2's to write in the same bullet.

All six proof legs green; test_sims_are_hermetic plus the seven other sims touching role files also pass.

payload.author: impl:2@run-155
payload.body: Task 2 approach: (1) module-level in fleet/run-engine.mjs — export `handshakeOf(issue)` (well-formed post or null), plus `handshakeFault`, canonical-JSON sha256 and the first-differing-cell renderer, dropped in after `stateExamBlock`. (2) M1 — per-task seeding in runTaskInner: producers come off the run's dependency edges (`predecessorsOf`, falling back to the `a -> b` strings), one fresh `kataCall('getissue')` per producer (the Setup read predates the post, so it cannot carry it), `content` written compact to `state-exams/posted/<producer>.json` in both the task clone and the examiner's, seeded at the end of `cutExamClone` and again for the graded clone before the pair is dispatched — i.e. before any exam command of the task runs. The seed path is added to each clone's `.git/info/exclude` so `git add -A` never folds run-local state into the target. (3) M2 — a `handshakeCheck()` at the tail of `prePass()`: reads the task's own issue, compares the parsed `expected` file in the graded clone with `content`, appends `handshake:settled` when equal and otherwise pushes one red whose line is the `handshake:` finding, which is what buys the `fix:<id>:0` round. (4) findings are recorded per task and surface as a new `tasks[].findings` key on the report row (`{severity, actor, detail}`), deduped by detail, beside one `handshake:finding` event. (5) `fact:state.reached {task, expected, sha256}` is appended once per post (deduped by task+sha256), so a post read at both M1 and M2 is one event. Everything is gated on `kataOn`, and no prompt-building code is touched.

payload.author: exam:2@run-155
payload.body:
examiner (task 2, the state handshake): approach before the long stretch.

The exam lands at `fleet/tests/exams/run_155/test_run_engine_state_handshake.mjs` (EXAM PATHS), so every relative import is written for that depth — `../../../run-engine.mjs` is the engine, `../../_engine_helpers.mjs` the rig.

Shape: one engine sim per leg, on the same two-task plan — producer `1`, consumer `2`, edge `1 -> 2` (the consumer's `Consumes:` edge the compiler emits), a fake hub of the `makeFakeKata` shape copied from `test_worker_kata_env.mjs`/`test_run_engine_kata_landing.mjs`, and a stub worker seam. The consumer's Proof path is a shell exam the examiner stub writes into its own clone; its command records what it can read of `state-exams/posted/1.json` into a witness directory under `$ULTRA_RUN_DIR`, at both passes the driver runs it (`base` in `clones/exam-2`, `0` in `clones/task-2`) — that is leg (a)'s 'measured by an exam command that reads the file', and it is how 'before the exam command first runs' is read as a fact about the moment rather than about the tree afterwards.

Three readings I am writing the file on, recorded here because a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct them:

1. The post is written by the producer's IMPLEMENTER, during its session (the global constraint says so), so the stub writes `state.reached` into the fake's store as the `impl:1` session ends — not into the issue at setup. The driver's Setup-time `getIssue` (`openKataTask`) therefore cannot be the read M1/M2 name; the handshake needs a read of its own. That write does not bump the fake's revision, exactly as the attention-hook's write does not in the landing sim.
2. M3's 'every post the driver reads under M1 or M2 is appended once' is read as once per POST, not once per read: in the leg (a)/(c) run the same post is read twice (the consumer's seed, the producer's pre-review compare) and the exam asserts EXACTLY ONE `fact:state.reached`.
3. M2's detail names 'the first differing cell'. The fixtures differ in exactly ONE cell, so the cell named is the same under any traversal order — the exam pins the detail string, not an iteration order the clause never fixes. That cell's value is a boolean, so `true`/`false` renders the same under `String` and `JSON.stringify` and the detail is unambiguous.

Leg (h)'s 'byte-identical to the prompt the same run produces at BASE' is measured by importing the BASE engine out of a `git worktree` cut at  and running the same plan through it, in the same run-directory path (the first run's tree is removed and re-provisioned) so the patch paths the reviewer prompt carries are identical by construction; both engines are handed the same `rolesDir`, so a sibling's role-file edit cannot move the comparison.

payload.author: exam:2@run-155
payload.body:
Exam landed at fleet/tests/exams/run_155/test_run_engine_state_handshake.mjs (nothing at the Proof path). Red at BASE for one reason: run-engine.mjs exports no `handshakeOf`, so the named import does not link.

How I checked it is red only for that reason: a throwaway copy with a local `handshakeOf` and a soft `assert` ran all nine sim runs end to end — 36 assertion failures, every one of them a handshake claim, and not a single `sim precondition` assertion among them. So the rig itself is green at BASE; only the feature is missing. 5.5s wall clock.

Four readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. The post is written mid-session by the PRODUCER'S IMPLEMENTER (the run's constraint says so: `kata meta set state.reached --json-value` on its own issue). The fake hub's `post()` sets the metadata without recording a call and without bumping the revision — so the driver's Setup-time `getIssue` in `openKataTask` cannot be the read M1/M2 name, and a fresh read is forced. Same trick the landing sim uses for the attention hook's SessionEnd write.

2. M3's "appended once" is read as once per POST, not once per READ. Run A reads the same post twice — to seed the consumer under M1, to compare under M2 — and the exam asserts EXACTLY ONE `fact:state.reached`.

3. M2's "first differing cell": the fixture differs in exactly ONE cell, so no traversal order is pinned. That cell holds a boolean (`todos/0/completed`, posted true / file false) so the detail has one spelling under `String` and under `JSON.stringify`: `handshake: todos/0/completed got true wanted false`.

4. `blocking` + `actor: implementer` are asserted through the routing the clause itself defines ("routed to `fix:<id>:0` exactly as any blocking finding"), because the engine keeps no per-task findings array a sim can read. So: exactly one `- handshake: ...` line in the `fix:1:0` prompt's blocking block, the same one line in the `review round 0:` comment the driver posts on the producer's issue, the same in the failed row's notes, the row `failed` with no referee dispatched — and, for `implementer` and not `plan`, no `plan-defect` entry in `deferredVerification` and no `actor: plan` on the row.

Two more mechanics worth knowing:
- Leg (a)'s "measured by an exam command that reads the file" is a real shell Proof the examiner stub writes; its command copies `state-exams/posted/1.json` into `$ULTRA_RUN_DIR/witness/<task>-<pass>/` at both passes (`base` in clones/exam-2, `0` in clones/task-2), and records `pwd` so the exam proves which clone each pass ran in. It always exits 0, so a missing seed is recorded rather than turned into a red that would reshape the run.
- Leg (h) imports the BASE engine out of `git archive 901fc874` into a temp tree and runs the same plan through it, same repo, same runDir PATH (so patch paths in the reviewer prompt match by construction), with both engines handed the same temp `rolesDir` (no role file of the checkout — one of which task 1 is editing — can move the comparison). `GIT_AUTHOR_DATE`/`GIT_COMMITTER_DATE` are pinned for the process, without which wave 2's BASE is a timestamped fold sha and three prompts differ. Verified: 0 byte diffs across all five prompt files.

Leg (i) is read as "the client is handed over but the record is not" — that is what `--kata` absent means to the engine (`kataOn` needs both halves), and it is the only way to COUNT zero `getIssue` rather than merely not observe one. That leg is necessarily green at BASE; M4 says as much ("behaves exactly as at BASE").

Nothing unsatisfiable. All nine legs plus a direct unit block on `handshakeOf` itself (M5's well-formedness, both malformed halves, and the fact that a third key does not make a value malformed).

payload.body:
Task 2 (the driver's two reads) is implemented and green.

Design decisions a later session would otherwise rediscover:

1. Both handshake reads are FRESH `kataCall('getissue', …)` calls, not the cached Setup read. `openKataTask` runs for every task in Setup (run-engine.mjs, `for (const t of WAVES.flat()) await openKataTask(t)`), which is before any worker — so the cached issue cannot carry a `state.reached` a worker wrote. The handshake read also deliberately skips `openKataTask`'s revision-mismatch fatal: a producer's own `--json-value` write bumps the revision, and that must not kill the run.

2. Seeds must not ride the captured patch. `patchAgainstBase` stages with `git add -A`, so an untracked `state-exams/posted/1.json` would land in the fold and on the target. Every seeded clone gets `state-exams/posted/` appended to its `.git/info/exclude` before the file is written.

3. Seeding the examiner's clone is folded into `cutExamClone` itself, because that function `rm -rf`s the exam dir and runs a second time for the #762 examiner-alone re-dispatch — seeding once outside it loses the file.

4. M3 says a post is appended 'once'; leg (g) says 'every read post yields exactly one'. Resolved by deduping `fact:state.reached` on `<task>|<sha256>`, so a post read at M1 (seeding) and again at M2 (the producer's pre-review pass) is one event. `handshake:absent` dedupes on `<task>|<producer>`, `handshake:settled` on `<task>|<sha256>`, and findings on their detail — prePass runs twice when a fix round is bought.

5. Two sims outside FILES had to move: `test_run_engine_reuse.mjs` and `test_worker_kata_env.mjs` each asserted 'exactly one getIssue per task' over the WHOLE run. The handshake adds one read per task inside the wave, which those clauses were never about (they are about the setup read that checks the revision and takes the fact sheet / the short id). Both are now measured over the reads that precede the first dispatch, which is what the clause text says. Declared as an amendment (amends: files).

6. `skills/ultrapowers/references/report-format.md` is NOT updated for the new `tasks[].findings` row key — out of FILES, and the schema there has no `additionalProperties`, so nothing breaks; raised as a concern instead.

Proofs green: `test_run_engine_state_handshake.mjs` (10 legs) and `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` (40 sims swept, 0 offenders). The whole `fleet/tests/test_*.mjs` sweep is green too.

payload.author: fix:2:0@run-155
payload.body:
fix round 0 (task 2), approach before the work.

Both blocking issues are about WHERE the exam lives, not about the handshake itself: the peer's exam at `fleet/tests/exams/run_155/test_run_engine_state_handshake.mjs` is GREEN on this tree (4.6s, ALL TESTS PASSED, all ten legs), and `driver:exam-run` recorded exit 0 at round 0. So M1–M5 are satisfied; what fails is the tree around the exam.

1. Proof `Run:` — `node fleet/tests/test_run_engine_state_handshake.mjs` is MODULE_NOT_FOUND because the handoff does exactly what it says it does: run-engine.mjs ~2889, `for (const [p] of examMoves) await restoreToBase(cloneDir, p)` — 'the Proof path is put back to BASE wherever the exam landed somewhere else … and nothing at the path the Proof named'. At BASE that path did not exist, so it is deleted. Meanwhile `examRunCmd` IS rewritten through `examMoves` (~2411) and `proofRuns` is NOT (~2952, the cmd runs verbatim) — so for any task whose exam moves under #890, the plan's own `Run:` line is guaranteed red. That is an engine defect, but fixing it in MY tree cannot fix THIS round: the driver re-runs the command with the checkout's engine, not mine. Fix: put a file back at the Proof path — inside FILES — that is a one-line static `import` of the landed exam, so the Proof command measures the peer's exam byte for byte rather than a second copy of it. Not a spawn (a spawn with a `test_*.mjs` literal would be named by the hermetic sweep's sibling rule), not a duplicate.

2. Global Constraints `Check:` — `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` names exactly two offenders, both in the peer's exam: `exams/run_155/…:722` `execFileSync('git', […,'archive',BASE_SHA])` and `:724` `execFileSync('tar', …)`, each with no `env:`. The sweep reaches `exams/<slug>/test_*.mjs` by design (#890, its leg (j) pins the reach), so the exam is held to the same hermeticity rule as any sim, and it does not meet it. Nothing in run-engine.mjs can move a static read of the exam's source. Fix: add `env: simEnv()` to those two setup spawns and import `simEnv` from `../../_helpers.mjs` — the literal form the sweep accepts outright. No assertion, fixture or leg changes; `tar` and `git` both resolve on the PATH simEnv builds (/usr/bin). This IS an edit of a driver-owned exam and the drift check will record it as `examEdited`; declaring it as an amendment and as an `exam:` concern rather than hiding it, because the alternative is leaving a Global Constraint red over two lines of rig setup.

One set of assertions in the tree, the examiner's; the Proof path is a pointer to it, not a second copy. (2) two lines of the exam's leg (h) rig take `env: simEnv()` (+ one import), which is the literal form the sweep accepts.

Two things for whoever reads this next.

A. The exam edit is real and declared. `examEdited` will name `fleet/tests/exams/run_155/test_run_engine_state_handshake.mjs` on the row. It touches no assertion, no fixture, no leg — only the `env:` of the `git archive` and `tar` that build leg (h)'s BASE tree. There was no alternative: the sweep is a STATIC read of the exam's source, so no change to run-engine.mjs could have cleared it, and leaving it meant a Global Constraint red over two lines of rig setup. Also recorded as an `exam:` concern on the reply.

B. The engine defect behind issue 1 is still there, and it is not mine to fix from inside a clone. `examRunCmd` is rewritten through `examMoves` (run-engine.mjs ~2411) and `proofRuns` is not (~2952) — so every task whose exam moves under #890 gets a red Proof `Run:` from the driver, this round and every round, no matter what its implementer wrote. The shim makes THIS task's line green honestly; the general repair is to run `proofRuns` through the same `examMoves` rewrite `examRunCmd` gets, which is a change to the driver's Run:/Check: pass that several sims pin and is outside this task's five Machine clauses. Raised as a concern rather than taken.
